overview: This bill, called the American FIRST Act, would require the three main federal bank regulators, the Federal Reserve, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (which oversees national banks) and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC, which insures bank deposits), to report each year to Congress on their work with international financial groups. These include bodies such as the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and the Financial Stability Board, where regulators from many countries agree on common banking standards. Each annual report would list the groups the agency belongs to, who funds them, the positions the agency took and the meetings it attended, any standards adopted, and what U.S. rule changes would be needed to carry them out, including an analysis showing the benefits justify the costs. The Federal Reserve's vice chair for supervision would also have to testify about these international dealings in the twice-yearly hearings before Congress. As of February 25, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was awaiting a vote by the full House.
for: Supporters say Americans and their representatives should be able to see what positions U.S. regulators take in international forums, since standards agreed there can later become binding rules on American banks.
against: Critics say the detailed reporting adds paperwork for regulators and could make U.S. officials less effective in international negotiations if their positions and strategies must be laid out publicly.
